edition.intro: This week's edit is all about cozy knits, confident color, smart layers, and boots and trousers that earn their keep all winter long.

items.title: 36 Best Sweaters for Men 2025, According to GQ Editors
items.snippet: Looking to cozy up right this winter? From artful cashmeres to zippy cable-knits, these are the swaddliest layers on the market—plus everything you should know before buying one.
items.headline: A Guide to the Sweater Styles Worth Owning This Winter
items.summary: GQ's editors walk through the main sweater shapes, from the V-neck and crewneck to the cardigan, turtleneck, cable knit and Fair Isle, and explain what each one does best. The big idea is to choose with a purpose, whether you want a workhorse for most outfits or something with a bit more personality. They also say not to shy away from color instead of defaulting to heather gray.
items.tip: Swap your usual gray sweater for one in a color you love and wear it with a white tee peeking out at the neckline.

items.title: Red Jeans Are Easier to Style Than You Think—Here’s How Fashion Girls Are Wearing Them
items.snippet: These color pairings make bold red jeans surprisingly wearable.
items.headline: Red Jeans Are Easier to Style Than You Think
items.summary: Elle says red denim works like a neutral with some attitude, especially next to white, gray, brown, camel and purple. The trick is to let the jeans take center stage while everything else stays grounded. Looks range from a ruffled blouse to a camel coat with loafers, and even head-to-toe red balanced with neutral shoes and a neutral bag.
items.tip: Try red pants or jeans with a camel or gray layer and brown loafers or sneakers, and keep the rest quiet.

items.title: The Art of the Winter Layer
items.snippet: Use these cold-weather staples from The North Face for practical warmth with polished style.
items.headline: How to Layer for Winter, One Piece at a Time
items.summary: Harper's Bazaar breaks cold-weather dressing into steps: a simple base, a hero jacket, practical extras like gloves, and a beanie to finish. The point is that warmth and polish can go hand in hand when each layer has a job. Many of the picks are from one outdoor brand, but the framework works with whatever you already own.
items.tip: Build your next cold-day outfit in order, starting with a snug base layer, then your best coat, then a hat and gloves.

items.title: I'm the Fashion Editor My Friends Ask About Boots—These Are My Sale Picks
items.headline: A Fashion Editor's Boot Picks From the Early Sales
items.summary: A Marie Claire editor rounds up boots from many retailers, covering sleek black pairs, chocolate brown, suede, croc-embossed styles, cozy shearlings and sturdy moto or Chelsea boots. Prices range from budget-friendly to designer markdowns. She notes that trends like animal print and rich brown are strong this season, though stock tends to move fast.
items.tip: Before you buy a trendy boot, check whether it works with at least three outfits you already own.

items.title: The Best Boots Under $500—From Everyday Classics to Seasonal Statements
items.snippet: Shop the best boots under $500, whether you want a versatile ankle boot, a chic knee-high, or a grippy, weather-proof style.
items.headline: The Best Boots Under $500, Sorted by Style
items.summary: Vogue organizes its picks by type: ankle boots for everyday wear, knee-highs with skirts or tucked jeans, flat boots for walking, statement styles with a bit of personality, and weatherproof pairs for rain or snow. The goal is lasting quality in a timeless shape at a sensible price. Think about how you actually live before choosing which category to prioritize.
items.tip: Decide which boot type fits your daily routine, such as flat for walking or weatherproof for rain, and shop only that one.

items.title: 10+ Winter Looks to Recreate From Fashion’s Beloved Style Icons
items.snippet: From Lee Radziwill to Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy and Audrey Hepburn, 5+ winter outfit ideas to steal from fashion’s favorite muses.
items.headline: Winter Looks to Borrow From Fashion's Great Style Icons
items.summary: Vogue looks back at women like Jackie Kennedy Onassis, Audrey Hepburn, Princess Diana, Jane Birkin and Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy to show how timeless winter outfits come together. Common threads include versatile neutrals, a statement coat or belt, rich textures and a hat or gloves for polish. Many of these outfits rely on simple pieces worn with confidence.
items.tip: Pick one icon's formula, like a black V-neck with a cream skirt and brown boots, and rebuild it from your closet.

items.title: These $90 Corduroys Are So Buttery You Could Baste a Turkey With Them
items.snippet: I own more cords than any man should, and Banana Republic has done me dirty again.
items.headline: These Soft Banana Republic Corduroys Are Worth the Hype
items.summary: A GQ writer raves about Banana Republic's loose, pleated corduroys, praising their soft, substantial fabric and the way they drape and hold their shape. The straight leg and high-ish waist work with boots, derbies or dressier shoes, and the pants are warm and machine washable. At under $150, they are pitched as a real alternative to jeans on winter errands and nights out.
items.tip: Wear corduroy trousers instead of jeans one day this week, with a sweater and boots for an easy upgrade.

practice: Start by shopping your closet: pull out the sweaters, boots, trousers and coats you already own and look for combinations you haven't tried. A neutral knit with corduroy or red jeans, a camel or gray coat, and the boots you reach for most can make a handful of fresh outfits before you spend anything. Take cues from the style icons and stick to a tight palette of neutrals, then let one color or texture be the star.

If you do buy, make it one thing that fills a real gap, such as a well-made sweater in a color you love, a pair of cords, or a boot that suits your daily routine and weather. Watch for sales rather than chasing every trend, and choose pieces that work with at least three things you own. Finish with the practical layers, a hat and gloves, so your outfits look polished and keep you warm.
